title: Following the principles is not yet the same as having the judgment
answer: The skill is better at preventing bad interface decisions than at generating an authored visual experience. It preserves useful constraints, but turns some context-dependent choices into global restraint rules and asks agents to explain a direction before they have visually explored it. The resulting interfaces can be thoughtful and usable while their hierarchy, material treatment and character remain conventional.
qualification: This is a supported interpretation of this skill and these three runs, not a causal estimate of what any Browser Company designer would produce. Some apparent distance is appropriate: an ops-room board and an accessible banking flow should not inherit a consumer browser's visual language.

findings.title: Some source ideas became narrower rules
findings.strength: Direct textual mismatch; output effect plausible, not isolated
findings.observation: The skill specifies exactly one distinctive moment, one control per action, one filled surface at most, and personality that never shouts. Those are stronger universal constraints than the product evidence supports.
findings.mechanism: A restriction on learning unfamiliar mechanics has become a restriction on how much visual character an otherwise familiar workflow may have. Identity can therefore become one small accent inside an otherwise predetermined neutral interface.

findings.title: Reference study loses perceptual information
findings.strength: Confirmed process gap in the recorded runs
findings.observation: The skill explicitly asks for thinking rather than pixels. Its reference exit criterion is a list of borrowed principles. Recall's example says Dia research used search summaries; banking reports blocked reference sites, and the dashboard reports no live reference research.
findings.mechanism: Agents can satisfy the reference phase without studying the composition, edge relationships, relative scales or state changes that the brief is asking them to learn. A written reason for a choice does not establish that the choice looks or feels strong.

findings.title: The system is specified earlier than the visual search
findings.strength: Sequence confirmed; quality impact is an inference
findings.observation: The method moves from a named direction and one novelty moment into tokens and a guarded system. It requires multiple refinement rounds, but no rendered alternative composition. The recorded refinements mostly fix hierarchy, overflow, contrast and state bugs.
findings.mechanism: The easiest objective becomes making the first defensible composition consistent. A 15 px answer versus 13 px body can be perfectly on-system while giving the main answer little perceptual separation. The menu experiments test that local consequence without changing its identity or workflow.

findings.title: Object treatment is already present, but unevenly edited
findings.strength: Direct comparison plus controlled layout measurements
findings.observation: Our shift strip retains responsibility through preview, pending and accepted states; our SMS preview makes a real message recognizable without showing a usable example code. These are substantive design decisions. But the SMS is wrapped in another filled panel, narrowing it and pushing its safety headline down.
findings.mechanism: The missing craft is sometimes the relationship between existing pieces, rather than an extra visual flourish. Removing the wrapper improves width and rhythm while preserving every word, control and text size. Adding a generic inset card to the menu does not establish a better identity.

findings.title: Static compliance cannot establish the overall experience
findings.observation: The original rubric rewards ordered priorities, a named novelty moment, tokens, themes, state coverage and verification. Those are valuable, but do not independently test the strength of the composition, attachment to the product, or the quality of a complete interaction. Reduced-motion screenshots deliberately suppress part of that evidence.
findings.mechanism: A pass is evidence of the asserted property, not evidence that the result has Browser Company sensibility. The skill needs a perceptual and temporal comparison loop alongside its technical checks, with explicit permission to discard a polished direction.

hypotheses: More playfulness is the missing ingredient
Profile identity and recognizable objects support selective expression. Plain routing and signup controls, and later neutral group defaults, contradict a universal playfulness prescription.
A different typeface would fix the gap
The evidence supports stronger relationships between type sizes and roles, not a required font family. Keeping the menu's existing font already changes its focal hierarchy.
Several rules are more absolute than their evidence warrants. Yet the banking improvement removes a container, and extra dashboard separation costs visibility. Restraint itself is not the problem.
The outputs are only polished conventional interfaces

The dashboard restructures the information hierarchy; the menu keeps ownership honest until acceptance; banking avoids a sample-code trap. Those are thoughtful product decisions, even where visual character is modest.
The original shift strip already persists through meaningful states. It is a successful translation worth retaining. The weakness is inconsistent refinement and limited visual calibration.
Intentional imperfection or a universal signature aesthetic is required
Rotated component presentations are not evidence that ordinary product controls should be irregular. Arc, early Dia and later Dia differ; authorship should not become a mandatory stylesheet.

recommendations.title: Relax three absolute rules; keep the constraints that protect users
recommendations.change: Treat novelty as the cost of learning, not exactly one expressive treatment. Distinguish status semantics from color used for identity, content relationships or atmosphere. Judge surfaces by the object they express, not a fixed count.
recommendations.why: Directly addresses G1. The card and dashboard probes show why the replacement must be conditional, not a new pro-decoration rule.
recommendations.keep: Contrast, honest states, recognizable controls and safety requirements remain binding.

recommendations.title: Require visual evidence before claiming to borrow a team's judgment
recommendations.change: Study an ordinary state, a distinctive object and a state transition. Keep source crops and version dates. Record what is visually doing the work, what is merely presentation, and what the new product should deliberately do differently.
recommendations.where: method.md reference phase; new worked examples only after review
recommendations.why: Addresses the documented text-only reference gap. It makes reference study concrete without importing Dia's assets, palette or layout.
recommendations.keep: Borrow the decision and relationship; preserve the new product's brand and platform.

recommendations.title: Explore before guarding a system
recommendations.change: When direction is uncertain, render genuinely different compositions before choosing one. Compare focal hierarchy, density, the user-valued object and the resting state. Then write tokens for the selected direction; revisit them when the comparison exposes a weakness.
recommendations.where: method.md direction/system boundary; SKILL.md recommendation wording
recommendations.why: A verbal rationale and a swap test are weak proxies for visual quality. Presenting one recommendation does not require considering only one design.
recommendations.keep: Use tokens to preserve a good decision, not to protect the first decision from scrutiny.

recommendations.title: Review a short task journey as well as its screens
recommendations.change: Inspect before, during and after the meaningful action: selection, loading, pending, completion, return and reduced-motion fallback. Ask what remains recognizable and where attention travels. Keep optional complexity discoverable rather than permanently visible.
recommendations.why: Connects the useful object/state evidence to evaluation. Current CSS probes do not validate new choreography or long-term attachment; this needs a richer next experiment.
recommendations.keep: No delays, hidden essential information or gestures as the only path.

recommendations.title: Separate functional assurance from visual judgment
recommendations.change: Keep automated checks, then compare revisions blindly on coherence, focal hierarchy, appropriateness, recognizability of the important object and quality of the full task. Record mixed and losing results. Use similar tasks for preference judgments; treat cross-product examples as analogies.
recommendations.where: eval rubric and review workflow, rather than more stylistic prohibitions
recommendations.why: The current 100% pass rate cannot answer the central question. A single author reviewing their own interventions cannot validate a general skill improvement.
recommendations.keep: Do not turn a subjective preference into a measured performance claim or demand that a banking app look like a browser.

recommendations.title: Build a small, contrasting reference portfolio
recommendations.change: Include an expressive consumer workflow, an ordinary settings surface, a dense shared tool and an accessible flow. Show why different visual choices are appropriate, including one rejected experiment. Keep the portfolio small enough to compare rather than imitate.
recommendations.where: future references/case-*.md and visual evidence pack
recommendations.why: One enterprise side-panel case cannot carry the whole range of transferable judgment. Contrast teaches the boundary of a principle better than another universal rule.
recommendations.keep: Portability means shared quality of decisions, not a recognizable Browser Company skin.
